text:
nina: FYI: long-context generation shows quality collapse with int4 postnorm. Instead of a simple per-layer offset shim, proposing we evaluate a lightweight per-head dynamic scale annealing (D-SA) approach. cc @omar @kai

omar: explain D-SA in 1 line pls

nina: on each autoreg step compute a small running stat (mean abs activation) per head for the prefix, and slightly increase the dequant scale for heads where energy drifts down. This reduces asymmetric clipping without storing large float vectors.

kai: sounds fancy. ops tradeoffs? perf? memory?

nina: perf: a few extra fmuls per head per token (cheap on GPU kernels if fused). memory: only need scalar multipliers per head (float16/32), so tiny. Pros: adaptive to request; no per-layer length vectors. Cons: adds per-token compute, risk of oscillation if naive.

tess: how does this compare to the per-layer offset shim we discussed before?

nina: offset shim fixes a static bias learned from calib set. Works well for stable biases but doesn't adapt to input-dependent shifts (e.g., long prompts with semantic drift). D-SA adapts online per-request, so it can handle prefix-specific energy changes. Could also combine both: static offset + dynamic anneal.

omar: need safety: avoid runaway scaling. propose clip bounds [0.9, 1.1] and an exponential smoothing with alpha=0.1. Also require min_head_energy before applying.

kai: telemetry ideas?

nina: add `head_scale_multiplier` trace per request (sampled), `generation_entropy_delta`, `head_energy_prefix_mean`. Canary logic: if D-SA reduces longctx_quality_delta by >0.02 vs baseline int4, keep; if increases latency >1.5% or increases token_repeat_rate -> rollback.

tess: how to test for oscillation?
nina: synthetic test: generate inputs with alternating high/low energy segments to ensure multiplier converges and doesn't oscillate across tokens. Add unit test for smoothing behavior and end-to-end test comparing BLEU/ROUGE on our long-dialog corpus.

omar: fallback policy: if any head multiplier hits clamp more than 10% of tokens in 1k window, mark request degraded and route remainder of request to int8. Also emit `head_scale_clamp_rate` metric and alert on >2% sample rate.

kai: implementation path: 1) microbenchmark kernel cost (fused dequant + scale) 2) implement CPU/GPU shim + smoothing 3) small canary (1% long requests mirrored) 4) dashboard + alerts.

ops-bot: Canary scheduled: shadow-dsa-int4 on prod-dedicated @ 06/20 01:00 UTC (1% mirror sampling)

omar: lifecycle: D-SA config must be tied to profile version and invalidated on model weight updates. Add `dsa_version` and `dsa_params` to profile blob. Also add lint preventing enabling without canary history.

tess: also consider hybrid: for very narrow layers or tiny heads noise dominates, prefer static offset or route to int8. Add `min_head_dim` gate and `apply_if_head_energy > 1e-4`.

nina: good. next steps: nina -> kernel microbench + prototype, omar -> telemetry and alert rule, kai -> canary config + synthetic tests. ETA 10 days. I'll file RFC follow-up summarizing playbook + rollback steps.
